issue_context.title: Duplicate Declaration Function should be Overwritten but get Duplicate binding Error
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

The function repeatedly declared in the JavaScript scope will be overwritten by the last function, however, the program can still run correctly, but the error of duplicate binding is reported during SWC conversion.

### Input code

```typescript
function sum ( i, j) {
  return i + j;
}

function sum(){
  return 0;
}

console.log(sum());
console.log(sum(1, 2));
```


### Config

```json
{
  "jsc": {
    "parser": {
      "syntax": "ecmascript",
      "jsx": false,
      "dynamicImport": false,
      "privateMethod": false,
      "functionBind": false,
      "exportDefaultFrom": false,
      "exportNamespaceFrom": false,
      "decorators": false,
      "decoratorsBeforeExport": false,
      "topLevelAwait": false,
      "importMeta": false
    },
    "transform": null,
    "target": "es5",
    "loose": false,
    "externalHelpers": false
  }
}
```


### Playground link

https://play.swc.rs/?version=1.2.148&code=H4sIAAAAAAAAA0srzUsuyczPUyguzVXQUMjUUcjSVKjmUlAoSi0pLcpTyFTQVsiy5qrl4kpDUqmhiaTEACydnJ9XnJ%2BTqpeTn64BVqFpjSFmqKNgBBQHAM2STN90AAAA&config=H4sIAAAAAAAAAy2LQQqAMAwE%2F5KzVy%2F9g48INUpL05YkgkX6dw142t0Z9oGsEcIDHUVJvOmohjcEoMioUVI3mAsYyknmWFff3ParkB9s9C8hNuZWs7pMuv36wKI0X3tLUmhnAAAA

### Expected behavior

After SWC conversion, the code does not change the semantics, and the last function with the same name overwrites the previous function

### Actual behavior

_No response_

### Version

1.2.148

### Additional context

I run swc use cmd as follows
```bash
npx swc --config-file=.swcrc poc.js -o poc.js
```
The environment is ubuntu 20.04 amd64.
comments: This is expected behaviour for `module` source type but we need to allow this for `script`
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.

review_comments: This is not correct, because `var` can override anything.

It's not true in module.
I have tested this locally with the following code.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  </head>
  <body>
    <script>
      var x = 1;
      var x = 2;
      function x() {}
      function x() {} // ok
    </script>

    <script type="module">
      var foo = 1;
      var foo = 2; // ok

      function foo1() {}
      function foo1() {} // error
    </script>

    <script type="module">
      var bar = 1;
      function bar() {} // error
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

Oh... So `three.js` should be treated as a script?

https://github.com/swc-project/swc/runs/5442747097?check_suite_focus=true
I agree. It should be treated as script.
